quizzes.stem: A user asks an assistant to count how many times a particular letter appears in a long product identifier and gets a wrong, confident number. What explains the failure, and what is the sound remedy?

options.a: The model sees sub-word pieces, so exact tallies belong in code
options.b: The window ran out, so the code should be shortened
options.c: The sampler was too cold, so it should be raised
options.d: The weights were stale, so the model should be retrained

explanation.a: The tokenizer section explains that the model works on pieces, not letters, so character-level tallies are approximate; code counts exactly (the first trap).
explanation.b: Ruled out because a short code fits any window and the error is not a cut-off.
explanation.c: Ruled out because sampling temperature changes variety, not letter-level access.
explanation.d: Ruled out because retraining does not change how text is cut into pieces for a given model.

quizzes.stem: A team says: "Our assistant made the same mistake in forty chats last week, so after we corrected it in chat it should now know better." Which statement is accurate?

options.a: Corrections in a conversation update its weights for later sessions
options.b: Corrections persist only if the API temperature is lowered
options.c: Corrections apply within that conversation's context only
options.d: Corrections are saved once the model is fine-tuned by default

explanation.c: What looks like learning is the context window; weights are fixed at inference (the weights section).
explanation.a: is ruled out for the same reason.
explanation.b: Ruled out because temperature has no storage role.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the glossary says the API does not currently offer fine-tuning and, in any case, fine-tuning is a deliberate separate process.

quizzes.stem: A stakeholder asks why the assistant answers questions helpfully, when a raw pretrained model would often just continue the text. Which stage does the most to explain the difference?

options.a: A larger vocabulary in the tokenizer
options.b: Further training on curated examples and ranked human preferences
options.c: A wider context window at inference time

explanation.b: Fine-tuning and feedback training turn a text continuer into an assistant (the stages section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a tokenizer only cuts text; it does not teach instruction following.
explanation.c: Ruled out because window size is a capacity, and a raw model with a big window still continues text.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the sampler picks among the model's options and does not create the helpful behaviour.

quizzes.stem: A company wants Claude to answer from its product manual, which changes monthly. A colleague proposes fine-tuning the model on each new manual. What is the best response?

options.a: Agree, because only weights can store product facts
options.b: Ask the model to memorise the manual in chat
options.c: Agree, but only after lowering the temperature
options.d: Place the latest version in the prompt instead

explanation.d: Weights are changed by training, a separate act that the API does not currently offer, and knowledge that changes monthly belongs in the context (the trap on fine-tuning and the table).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table shows knowledge can live in the window too.
explanation.c: Ruled out because temperature is irrelevant to where facts are stored.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a conversation does not change the weights, so nothing is memorised for later.

quizzes.stem: An analyst complains that Claude "forgot" the glossary they taught it last week in a separate session. Which explanation fits how models are made?

options.a: Weights stay fixed at inference, so each conversation starts fresh
options.b: The tokenizer drops terms that were unfamiliar the first time
options.c: Attention discards any term older than seven days
options.d: Constitutional training deletes user vocabulary overnight

explanation.a: Weights do not change while you chat, so a new conversation has no trace of the old one (page 1, weights section).
explanation.b: Ruled out because tokenizers cut text and store nothing about a user.
explanation.c: Ruled out because attention weighs positions within the current context only, with no clock.
explanation.d: Ruled out because constitutional training happens before release and holds no user vocabulary.

quizzes.stem: A localisation lead notices that the same paragraph needs noticeably more tokens in one language than in another. What is the most likely reason?

options.a: The two languages were assigned different context windows
options.b: The model refuses one language in order to save money
options.c: The tokenizer's learned pieces match one writing system better
options.d: RLHF raises the price of less common languages

explanation.c: Learned sub-word pieces were built from a corpus, so some languages split into more pieces (page 1, "what the tokenizer does to your work").
explanation.a: Ruled out because the window is a model property, not set per language.
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing on the pages describes any such refusal.
explanation.d: Ruled out because feedback training shapes behaviour and does not set token counts.

quizzes.stem: A teammate says a model's answer must be right because it was trained to be honest. Which reply is accurate?

options.a: Honesty training makes every figure verified
options.b: That is a goal of training; check important claims anyway
options.c: Honesty training only applies to harmful topics
options.d: Honesty training is replaced by the system prompt

explanation.b: The glossary frames HHH as a training framework and goal, and the traps say verification is still needed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because nothing in training verifies figures.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the framework covers accuracy as well as harm.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a system prompt steers behaviour at run time and does not replace training.

quizzes.stem: Which task is the poorest fit for a model working alone, given how tokenizers and training work?

options.a: Summarising a meeting transcript in three bullets
options.b: Explaining a stack trace in plain language
options.c: Suggesting five names for a new internal tool
options.d: Reporting the exact number of characters in a string

explanation.d: Exact character counts are a tokenizer-level weakness, so code should do them (page 1).
